default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1008.title: Same-minute forward-drift seasonality
E-1008.hypothesis: Order flow tied to the clock (index rebalancing, ETF/institutional schedules) repeats at the same time of day; when the 20-session average forward move from this minute is consistently one-signed, trade it.

E-1009.title: US-open anchor impulse follow
E-1009.hypothesis: The US cash open (10:30 or 11:30 Brasilia time depending on DST) brings foreign flow; a move away from the price at that anchor larger than usual shows that flow is directional, so follow it.

E-1010.title: Variance-ratio trending regime follow
E-1010.hypothesis: When 4-bar return variance exceeds 4x the 1-bar variance, returns are positively autocorrelated (trend regime, herding stops and momentum orders); follow the direction of the latest 4-bar move.

E-1011.title: Bollinger band re-entry fade
E-1011.hypothesis: A close outside the Bollinger band that returns inside on the next bar is a failed extension; the late breakers are trapped and price tends to go back toward the mean.

E-1012.title: Session-range midpoint cross follow
E-1012.hypothesis: After price spent a long time on one side of the day's range midpoint, a close through it moves the fair-value reference of the session; the side that lost it must cover or liquidate, so follow.

E-1013.title: Persistent up-bars without progress fade
E-1013.hypothesis: When most bars of the window close up yet the net move is small, passive sellers are absorbing the buying with limit orders; the stalled side gives up, so fade it (mirror for down bars).

E-1014.title: Lunch-range break follow
E-1014.hypothesis: From about 12:00 to 14:00 B3 liquidity is thin and the range compresses; the first close beyond the lunch high/low after 14:00 (US data, afternoon desks back) releases stops and starts the afternoon trend.

E-1015.title: Momentum acceleration follow
E-1015.hypothesis: A move whose latest leg is much faster than the previous leg of the same length shows new aggressive participants joining; momentum followers and stops add to it, so follow the acceleration.

E-1016.title: RSI extreme re-entry fade
E-1016.hypothesis: An RSI that was beyond 70/80 and falls back below the threshold shows the push is losing its buyers; the first re-entry marks the turn, so trade against the prior extreme (mirror at 30/20).

E-1017.title: Largest-bar climax fade
E-1017.hypothesis: When the current bar is the largest-bodied bar of the last hour(s) and far above normal size, it is typically forced flow (stops, market orders) at the end of a move; liquidity providers lean against it.
